stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV: AI doom fears are not ‘fake news’
stories.deck: The first U.S. pope, who has warned of the dangers of AI throughout ‌his 16-month papacy, also directly criticized technology CEOs who argued there should be ‌no guardrails on the technology.
stories.bodyText:
Pope Leo on Monday (September 28, 2026) said concerns that artificial intelligence could destroy the world are not “fake news” and should be taken seriously, in an apparent rebuke of U.S. President Donald Trump.
The first U.S. pope, who has warned of the dangers of AI throughout his 16-month papacy, also directly criticized technology CEOs who argued there should be no guardrails on the technology.
“I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously,” the pontiff said in a press conference on his flight back to Rome after a four-day trip to France. “I don’t think that that is fake news, as some have said.”
Mr. Trump told the U.N. General Assembly last week that he believed fears about the dangers to humanity from AI were a “hoax.”
The pope said he had read on Monday (September 28) that the head of chipmaker Nvidia had announced there could be a way to insert guardrails into certain AI models. But Pope Leo expressed scepticism, adding: “He’s the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation.”
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang told CBS News this month that he agreed with Mr. Trump that safety concerns about AI were overblown.
Pope Leo urged the world “to promote dialogue, study, investigate, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity.”
“I think that there are enough people seriously interested in that … but we have to keep working,” said the Pope. “We can’t just sit back and pretend nothing’s going to happen.”

stories.headline: PMO reviews Ambedkarite writings in university curricula after anonymous post calls them ’poison’
stories.deck: Academic Kancha Ilaiah Shepherd questions the interference of the PMO in the syllabus of universities, which ought to be in the purview of the Department of Higher Education or University Grants Commission
stories.bodyText:
Works of prominent intellectuals and academics recommended as readings in several higher learning institutions are under the scanner of the Higher Education Department, following an enquiry by the Prime Minister’s Office, which was triggered by an anonymous social media post terming these works ‘poison’. The authors/editors of the works include B.R.Ambedkar, Jyoti Rao Phule, Gail Omvedt, Braj Ranjan Mani, and Sharmila Rege, among others.
An urgent online missive from the department to all the central universities on Sunday (September 27, 2026) referred to communication received from the PMO regarding the post and sought their ‘comments’. Further, the email sought details about enrolment in the courses mentioned in the post.
“All the Central Universities are requested to furnish comments on the above. Further, enrollment in the courses mentioned in the tweet may also be apprised to the Ministry [sic],” the communique said, before marking the matter as ‘Urgent’, and seeking the comments/information ‘at the earliest’.
The post/tweet was shared on the platform X on September 26, 2026. It read:“THIS IS WHAT STUDENTS ARE BEING TAUGHT AT OUR UNIVERSITIES
From patriarchy to Caste Annihilation to Debrahmanising the history to Curse of Manu we are feeding young minds with a poison which our leftist cabal use a apprenticeship for grooming their future rank and file [sic]” the post said, looping in a thread of six more posts on the subject.
Attached to the post was an image with a list of 35 works-- notably even Ramayana and Mahabharata-- while the extended thread singled out the works: Annihilation of Caste by B.R. Ambedkar, Against the Madness of Manu: B.R. Ambedkar’s writings on Brahminical Patriarchy’ compiled by Sharmila Rege, ‘Ghulamgiri’ by Jyotirao Phule, ‘Debrahmanising History: Dominance and Resistance in Indian Society’ by Braj Ranjan Mani, ‘Dalits and Democratic Revolution’ and ‘Towards a Historical Materialist Analysis of the Origins and Development of Caste’ both by Gail Omvedt, ‘Mahishasur, Ek Jananayak’ and ‘Mahishasur: Mithak aur Paramparayen’ by Pramod Ranjan, ‘Bharat Ke Moolnivasi aur Arya-Akraman’ by Swapan Kumar Biswas, ‘Bharat Ke Moolnivasi: Rigvedic Asur aur Sharanagat Arya’ by S.L.Nirmohi. Besides, the post mentions Bhikku Bodhanand as the godfather of the anti-Brahmin thesis in leftist academic circles.
It concludes by saying, “So, if you wonder who created Kanhaiya Kumar or Neha Bora? It is our education system, infested with such books and anti-Hindu propaganda propagated by left-leaning teachers who are also products of the same education system. We need to break this cycle.”
Interestingly, none of these writers mentioned in the post could be characterised as left-leaning. On the contrary, several of them critiqued traditional Indian left from the perspective of caste and gender.
“Ambedkarism was always opposed to the leftist idea of class war. If the PMO stands for opposing Phule, Ambedkar being taught, then it stands against SC/ST/OBCs when the PM himself is an OBC and the President is ST. If the PMO stands for Patriarchy and Manudharma, then it is against man-woman equality,” observed writer and academic Kancha Ilaiah Shepherd, whose three works, including the trailblazing ‘Why I am not a Hindu ’, were listed among the 35 readings attached with the post.
He also questions the interference of the PMO in the syllabus of universities, which ought to be in the purview of the Department of Higher Education or University Grants Commission.
Apart from Mr. Shepherd, the authors whose works were mentioned in the image include E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar), R.S.Sharma, Savitribai Phule, Uma Chakravarti, Suvira Jaiswal, Aloka Parasher, Shireen Ratnagar, G. Aloysius, and Anupama Rao. Their works were cited as prescribed readings for postgraduate and undergraduate studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Central University of Punjab, Delhi University, and Asutosh College affiliated to University of Calcutta.

stories.headline: Dhaka begins search for missing Assam woman
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum, who was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India on the case.
Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, additional secretary (Political and Immigration), Bangladesh home ministry, whose office deals with border enforcement, illegal crossings and cross-border deportations, said officials were trying to locate Mumtaz but had no information as of Sunday. The matter was sent to police and other depts late on Sept 27, days after TOI reached out.
Gauhati HC on Sept 3 directed MEA to "endeavour to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back". The HC also directed Assam govt to pay her husband Mujammel Hoque Rs 2 lakh interim compensation, observing "she was expelled without her husband or an adult family member being informed". HC found it denied her a chance to challenge it, a violation of democratic due process.
Tribunal declared Assam woman a foreigner, but Gauhati HC set it aside
Underscoring that basic human rights extend to anyone on Indian soil, the bench directed Assam Police and home dept to "ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed about tribunal orders and that their adult family members are notified before they are moved outside their district". 
The court criticised the tribunal for stripping her of the "opportunity to challenge the Foreigners Tribunal's opinion before Gauhati HC".
With no information in India, TOI contacted journalists, human-rights activists, officials and govt and security establishment sources across Bangladesh, focusing on Sylhet division and adjoining districts, where she could have ended up.
A senior Dhaka-based businessman, who wishes to stay anonymous, joined authorities in the search and is working with govt and security contacts. An appeal with her photo and identification details, including Foreigners Identification Portal ID, was published in prominent Bengali newspapers on Sept 22. Bangla daily Manob Kantha also carried her photo and reported on the family's search.

Official efforts in Sylhet, however, have found no lead. Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sarwar Murshed Shamim said police had "tried to locate Mumtaz within the metropolitan area but had not found her and were continuing the search."
Mumtaz, from Nagaon, was declared a foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal. The HC set aside the opinion and ordered fresh consideration, finding deficiencies in its assessment of evidence including 1965 and 1970 voter-list records of her grandfather, her father's 1977 voter-list record and voter ID, Gaonburah and Gaon Panchayat certificates, a school transfer certificate and land records.
She appeared before the tribunal on May 30 with her lawyer, after which police took her into custody. She was taken to Juria and Nagaon Sadar police stations, Matia holding centre in Goalpara, then Eraligool holding centre in Sribhumi (June 4-13).
Handed to BSF on June 13, she was sent to Bangladesh on June 14 from Kalaincherra, Cachar, BSF told the HC. Three months on, police, authorities and civil-society members are trying to establish where she is.

briefs.headline: Asian Games 2026 India’s medallists: Full list of winners
briefs.deck: Here’s the full list of Indian medallists at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 categorised by sport
briefs.bodyText:
The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are underway in Japan. India is currently placed at the 12th spot on the medals’ table with 46 medals. China is leading the table with 232 medals. Japan is second with 172 medals and Republic of Korea is third with 91 medals.
On September 28, 2026, Vithya Ramraj won a bronze medal in 400 M hurdles in a sensational run that clocked 54.75 seconds and broke her own national record she had jointly held with athlete PT Usha.
Murali Sreeshankar and Gulveer Singh claimed silver medals in the long jump and 1500m, respectively, while Parul Chaudhary secured bronze in the women’s 5000m, adding a second medal to her Aichi-Nagoya campaign.
India also bagged two medals in the javelin throw, with Yash Vir Singh winning silver and Rohit Yadav taking bronze, behind Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga.
Earlier that day, Indian shooter Esha Singh clinched a silver medal in the women’s 25m pistol individual competition.
Pincky Balhara became the first Indian to win two Kurash medals at the Asian Games after clinching bronze on Monday (September 28, 2026), following a 0-5 semifinal defeat to South Korea’s Sumin Mo in the women’s 78kg event.
On Sunday (September 27, 2026), India’s Abhay Singh settled for an Asian Games silver medal after going down against Eain Yow Ng of Malaysia in the men’s singles final of the squash competition, and junior world champion Anahat Singh similarly secured a hard-fought Silver in the women’s singles final against Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam.
Harita Bhadra clinched bronze in the women’s 200m at the Asian Games. Long jumper Ancy Sojan secured silver in the women’s long jump, while Sarvesh Kushare claimed silver in the men’s high jump.
Tejaswin Shankar, meanwhile, secured his second Asian Games medal, winning bronze in the decathlon following the two-day competition.
Parul Chaudhary bettered her personal best on her way to bronze in the women’s 3000m steeplechase at the Asian Games.
On Saturday (September 26), India’s Sawan Barwal won a silver medal in the men’s marathon. India’s women’s kabaddi team extended their dominance at the Asian Games securing yet another gold medal after a thrilling 37-34 win over Iran in the finals. The men’s hockey team continued it’s winning streak, defeating Japan by 2-0, securing the semifinal berth in the big-ticket sports event.
Simultaneously, the squash squad led by teen-sensation Anahat Singh and Abhay Shetty in singles category stormed into the final game. The duo will be competing for a gold medal in their final game on Sunday.
Women’s 50m rifle 3P team comprising of Vidarsa Vinod, Ashi Chouksey, Tilottama Sen won the silver medal. Mixed squash doubles team including Joshana Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar clinched the bronze medal.
On Friday (September 25), the duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze medal in table tennis mixed doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.
Baranica Elangovan entered her name in the record books by winning a historic bronze medal for India in the women’s pole vault event at the Asian Games
Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh upgraded his Asian Games medal from bronze to silver in the men’s 10,000m.
India’s Manpreet Kaur clinched the bronze medal in women’s shot put competition of the Asian Games with an effort of 17.17m in Nagoya on Friday (September 25).
Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event. The Indian team, comprising Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudranksh Patil and Niraj Kumar, won silver in the men’s 50m rifle 3P team event.
The Indian 4x400m mixed relay quartet of Vishal T.K., M.R. Poovamma, Manu T.S. and Vithya Ramraj earned a silver medal in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium.
Manpreet Kaur clinched a bronze medal in the Women’s Shot Put final with a season-best throw of 17.17 meters.
The duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze in Table Tennis Mixed Doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.
Seema Kumari, competing in her first Asiad, won a bronze medal in the 10,000m at the Asian Games, 16 years after Preeja Sreedharan and Kavita Raut’s historic gold-silver double in 2010.
Manipur’s Naorem Roshibina Devi won her third consecutive Asian Games medal, clinching silver after losing to Zhang Xiaoyu in the women’s 60kg wushu final on Thursday (September 24, 2026).
Jay Meena secured India’s first-ever soft tennis medal at the Asian Games, fetching a bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals. Star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu completed her medal collection, winning a silver medal in the women’s 49kg event in the Asian Games.
Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty faltered against higher-ranked opponents as the Indian men’s team concluded with a bronze medal after losing 1-3 to their rivals, China, in the semifinals.
The Indian Women’s Cricket Team clinched a historic victory at the Karogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi. Facing off against Sri Lanka in a high-stakes final, the Women in Blue triumphed to secure India’s very first gold medal of the tournament.
Meanwhile, shooters have led the charge for India. The women’s skeet team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, won a bronze with a combined score of 331 here on September 23, 2026.
Experienced rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan played a starring role in the country’s double-silver haul in the women’s 10m air rifle competition. Elavenil, one of India’s most accomplished rifle shooters, helped the country secure silver in the team event along with Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod. She then went on to add an individual silver.
For the men’s side, teenager Himanshu Dhillon produced a superb performance to win silver, while former world champion Rudrankksh Patil clinched bronze as India secured two individual podium finishes in the men’s 10m air rifle event. The two then teamed up with Parth Mane to win another silver in the team event, finishing just behind China.
After an impressive start in shooting, India also managed to script history in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA), with Suchika Tariyal winning the nation’s first-ever bronze medal for MMA at the Asian Games.
A contingent of 501 Indian athletes, comprising 267 men and 234 women, is competing across 36 disciplines in the 2026 edition. Apart from shooting, athletics and archery too are expected to add to the medal tally. India is also defending both the men’s and women’s titles in cricket and kabaddi.

briefs.headline: States stumped as demography panel seeks religion-wise data on vehicles, schools, voters
briefs.deck: The panel has sought religion-wise data for past 15 years on birth and vehicle registrations, school enrolment and property transactions, as well as district-wise details of religious structures and unusual increases in Aadhaar, voter ID and ration card registrations; data not maintained on religious lines, officials say
briefs.bodyText:
State governments are unable to answer most of the queries posed by a high-level committee studying demographic changes, as government departments do not ordinarily maintain much of the information sought by the panel on a religion-wise basis.
The High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes (HLCDC) has sought religion-wise data for the past 15 years on birth and vehicle registrations, school enrolment and property transactions, as well as district-wise details of religious structures and unusual increases in Aadhaar, voter ID and ration card registrations. It has also sought intelligence assessments and commission reports on religious conversions among Scheduled Tribe communities, and details of operational detention centres, among other information.
State government officials told The Hindu that the set of 35 questions asked by the committee was difficult to answer, as the secular construct of the Constitution prohibited the collection of data under religious categories. Other than birth registration, where the religion of the newborn is mentioned on the certificate, and the number of undocumented migrants apprehended or deported, the religion-wise data on all other categories were unavailable, said officials.
States have been asked to collate data on Hindus, Sikhs, Christians, Muslims, Parsis and Buddhists in all the categories.
As the principal Opposition in 2006, the Bharatiya Janata Party opposed the Sachar Commission recommendations and questioned their constitutional validity, stating that they promoted religious quotas and were socially divisive. The commission was appointed by the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government in 2005 to examine the social, economic, and educational status of the Muslim community.
One of the questions of the HLCDC reads: “Details of districts showing unusual school enrolment trends inconsistent with historical birth rates, along with reasons”. Another seeks district-wise data on religious structures (temples, mosques, churches, etc.) established in the past 15 years, including details of any GIS mapping or other technology used for their identification.
The committee had also sought data on district-, religion-, and year-wise voter registration data of the last 15 years for individuals “without prior-generation birth certificates or familial legacy records, including observed trends and concentrations”.
The committee has sought district-wise data on changes in religious composition, particularly in cities, industrial centres, border districts, tribal areas and Fifth/Sixth Schedule areas. It has also asked for State studies, intelligence assessments, commission reports and White Papers examining demographic changes.
States have been asked for information on changes in the religious composition of Scheduled Tribe populations and any studies or intelligence assessments concerning religious conversion among tribal communities, including reasons, district-wise trends and actions taken.
Also sought was religion-wise and district-wise information on birth registrations, including delayed registrations and institutional/non-institutional births. It also sought data on unusual increases in Aadhaar enrolments, voter IDs and ration cards, and cases involving forged identity documents.
The questionnaire requested 15 years of religion-wise and district-wise data on transport and non-transport vehicle registrations, as well as unusual increases in commercial vehicle licences, particularly in border and highly urbanised districts.
The committee has asked for religion-wise details of property transactions and information on unusual land acquisition, demographic clustering and ownership patterns. Separate questions concern tribal land transfers, illegal transfers and encroachments in tribal and Scheduled Areas.
States have also been asked to provide information on religion-wise distribution of ration cards and school enrolments, fraudulent access to welfare schemes, unusual school-enrolment patterns, and government, private and religious educational institutions in tribal-dominated districts. The questionnaire also asks about GIS mapping of religious educational institutions, including madrasas.
States must also furnish information on detention centres, identification, detention and deportation/repatriation of undocumented migrants, cases involving forged documents, and cases linking illegal migrants with organised crime, human trafficking or narcotics offences. Another question deals with intelligence, technical and community mechanisms used to identify undocumented migrants.
The committee has also asked States what policy directives, executive orders or amendments to land and municipal laws they have introduced over the past 15 years to curb unauthorised migration and settlement. It has also sought suggestions on whether new legislation was required to strengthen surveillance and take action to “reverse abnormal religious demographic change”.
The HLCDC, led by a retired Supreme Court judge, Justice Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar, was constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs on May 26 to study the demographic changes arising from illegal immigration and other abnormal reasons, and to suggest measures to deal with these demographic changes.
The questionnaire seeks to collect information on five broad areas - demographic trends, migration, administrative challenges, institutional mechanisms, studies and measures adopted by States/UTs.
On May 27, the Supreme Court, while upholding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Bihar, said that the Election Commission of India (EC) was well within its authority to verify citizenship to the limited extent of determining inclusion or exclusion from the electoral roll. The court directed the EC to refer, within the next four weeks, the names of electors who were part of the 2003 electoral roll but were purged in the Bihar SIR on the grounds of being non-citizens, to the Centre for adjudication by a competent authority under the Citizenship Act,1955.
Government sources told The Hindu that the EC was yet to provide this data to the committee. The committee has so far visited the Jammu region in Jammu and Kashmir and plans to visit Maharashtra next.
“We are yet to receive response from the State governments. A meeting was held with the EC officials last week, they are however yet to provide the data on people excluded from SIR on the grounds of being suspected foreign nationals staying here illegally,” said a member of the committee on condition of anonymity. The EC did not respond to queries from The Hindu regarding the reasons for the delay in submission of the data to the committee.

briefs.headline: Trump unveils Essar’s new steel plant in Iowa
briefs.deck: Mesabi Metallics is building the plant with the aim of starting production by 2030, a White House official said.
briefs.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday (September 28, 2026) unveiled Essar Group’s plans to build a massive steel plant in Iowa, at an investment of $15 billion.
Mr. Trump made the announcement in the Oval Office with Essar Group co-founder Ravi Ruia and his son Rewant by his side.
"Today, we're thrilled to announce that Mesabi Metallics will be building the largest steel plant in American history in the great state of Iowa," Mr. Trump said.
Essar Group's Mesabi Metallics chairman, Rewant Ruia, thanked Mr. Trump “for bringing back the importance of building things in America.”
Mesabi Metallics is building the plant with the aim of starting production by 2030, a White House official said.
The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year and create as many as 1,750 permanent jobs in the state, the official said.
The plant will use iron ore from a new mine that the company invested $2.5 billion to build in Minnesota. The mine will produce about 7.5 million tonnes of iron per year and create about 350 jobs in the state, the White House official said, noting that it will be the first new iron mine in the U.S. in 50 years.
The mine is based in Minnesota’s Mesabi Iron Range, which stretches 80 to 100 miles and contributed about 60 per cent of total iron ore production in the U.S. during the 20th century.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; John Jovanovic, chair of the Export-Import Bank; and David Copley, senior director for Global Supply Chain, were among the other people present at the announcement.
“This plant will use the latest technology and will compete head-to-head with any steel plant in the world on size, quality and on cost,” Rewant Ruia said.

briefs.headline: SIR will unite Opposition, says Telangana CM Revanth
briefs.bodyText:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy drew a parallel between the 1928 anti-Simon Commission agitation and the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying a similar nationwide movement could emerge against the exercise in the coming days.
Addressing a conclave in New Delhi on the theme ‘India’s Next Chapter’, Mr. Revanth said, “Just as the country united under the slogan ‘Simon Go Back’, it will unite under the slogan ‘Sir Go Back’ in the coming days,” adding that leaders, including Mamata Banerjee, Sharad Pawar, Uddhav Thackeray and M.K. Stalin could come together on the issue.
The Chief Minister alleged that decisions relating to electoral rolls were being centralised with the Election Commission and claimed that artificial intelligence was being used in the process.
Attack on Centre over Telangana projects
Mr. Revanth Reddy also accused the Union government of not extending the same cooperation to Telangana that, he said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi received from the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh when Mr. Modi was Gujarat Chief Minister.
He alleged that files relating to the Regional Ring Road, metro rail expansion and other projects were pending with the Centre. He also alleged that investment opportunities, including a semiconductor project, were being shifted towards Gujarat.
“This is not a north-versus-south issue; it is becoming Gujarat versus the rest of the country,” he said.
On delimitation, Mr. Revanth argued that southern States could lose political representation if Lok Sabha seats were redistributed primarily on the basis of population. He also criticised what he described as the concentration of key Union Government portfolios in northern States and argued that southern States needed adequate political representation.
On welfare schemes, Mr. Revanth Reddy defended the Congress government’s guarantees in Telangana, saying political parties could not ignore welfare when competing with one another. At the same time, he said governments needed to balance welfare expenditure with funds required for development.

briefs.headline: Europe's biggest chip company sells nothing at home, ASML exec says
briefs.deck: ASML, Europe's biggest chip company, is currently selling no chipmaking machines in Europe, says executive Frank Heemskerk, blaming a lack of investment and zero new chip factories. As the US, China and India court ASML, the EU's Chips Act is falling short of its 2030 goal to double Europe's global chip market share. CEO Christophe Fouquet and CFO Roger Dassen have also warned Brussels over AI…
briefs.bodyText:
ASML, the Dutch company whose machines sit inside almost every advanced chip factory in the world, is currently selling none of them in Europe. Frank Heemskerk, the executive responsible for ASML's global public affairs, said the company has no chipmaking machine sales on the continent right now, simply because nobody there is building chip plants to put them in.
"We are not selling anything in Europe at all. That is because Europe is not investing, and no chip factories are being built here," Heemskerk said. He added that the United States, China and India are all trying to persuade ASML to expand its operations in their countries. The remark comes as the European Union works on a revision of its semiconductor law, and it puts a hard number on a problem Brussels has been circling for years: zero.
Europe's Chips Act has not delivered the chip factories it promised
The EU Chips Act took effect in 2023, shaped by the global chip shortage during the Covid-19 pandemic. Its headline goal was to double Europe's share of the global chip market by 2030.
That target now looks out of reach. The European Court of Auditors concluded last year that the EU is unlikely to hit it, and the law has done little to get new semiconductor factories built in Europe.
For ASML, the gap is commercial as much as political. The company is the only maker of the advanced lithography machines needed to produce the latest generation of chips. 
Customers like TSMC and Samsung Electronics use them to print transistor patterns onto silicon wafers, which makes ASML a key link in the supply chain behind today's AI chips.
The US, China and India are competing for ASML's chipmaking machines
While Europe sits out, other regions are spending heavily on domestic semiconductor industries. China alone was expected to account for more than 25% of ASML's total sales in 2025, according to Shen Bo, president of ASML China, who spoke last November.
India is part of the same race, with its first large chip plants coming up in Gujarat and Assam. The US, meanwhile, has for years pushed the Netherlands to block some of ASML's most advanced machine sales to China, a reminder that ASML's order book is shaped by geopolitics as much as by demand.
ASML's top executives have been warning Brussels for months
Heemskerk's comment is the latest in a string of pointed remarks from ASML's leadership. In January, CEO Christophe Fouquet told Europe to be "realistic" about tech sovereignty, arguing that the chip ecosystem is spread across the world and that some imports will always be needed. On the same day, ASML posted better-than-expected results and announced 1,700 job cuts.
Chief financial officer Roger Dassen went further in October 2025. He blamed EU regulation for driving AI talent abroad, saying a skilled engineer's first move is often "buying a ticket to Silicon Valley." ASML had just become the largest shareholder in French AI company Mistral with a €1.3 billion investment.
Heemskerk himself has said, quoting a former company executive, that it is easier to get a senior White House meeting than one with an EU commissioner.
ASML and Brussels are now looking at ways to boost demand for semiconductors and make supply chains more resilient. The fix Heemskerk points to has little to do with ASML itself. Europe's biggest chip company will find customers at home only when someone in Europe starts building a fab.

briefs.headline: 'I offered nothing’: Trump denies sanctions relief to Iran, bashes media report
briefs.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump on Monday denied offering Iran any concessions, after a report emerged that Washington was willing to provide sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds as part of a final agreement if Tehran makes “concrete progress” on the nuclear issue.
“I offered them NOTHING!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, rejecting the claim that his administration had offered Iran sanctions relief.
Trump calls the claim 'untrue'
He wrote, "Axios just released a story that “Trump” offered Sanctions Relief and Frozen Funds to Iran. This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING! Axios’ story, like most others, is a HOAX, used only for purposes of satisfying their Trump Derangement Syndrome. They should withdraw this fake story, IMMEDIATELY!"
Trump says Iran ‘overplayed its hand’
Trump told Axios on Sunday that he expected further talks with Iran to take place this week.
“They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make,” Trump said. “It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand.”
Trump had also rejected Iran’s latest proposal concerning the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, calling it “unacceptable”.
Trump calls the claim 'untrue'
The US official said Iran had indicated it was willing to show flexibility on nuclear issues, but the two sides remained divided over the timing of the commitments.

briefs.headline: Over 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network busted, 350 held across 15 States: Amit Shah
briefs.deck: The Centre has declared the Bhatti network a terrorist organisation, which is allegedly involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics; Bhatti is a Pakistani social media influencer
briefs.bodyText:
More than 40 modules linked to the Shahzad Bhatti network, allegedly involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics, have been busted and 350 people arrested across 15 States, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Monday (September 28, 2026).
Mr. Shah said more than 100 First Information Reports had been registered against members of the network and that the Union Government had declared the Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Bhatti is a Pakistani social media influencer.
Extradition Portal
Mr. Shah launched a new Extradition Portal, which, according to the Home Ministry, is intended to coordinate and expedite efforts to bring fugitives back to India from abroad. He asked State police forces to form dedicated teams that could work with the Central agencies on extradition and other mechanisms for securing the return of fugitives.
He was speaking at the inauguration of a conference on ‘PRAHAAR – Counter Terrorsim Policy and Strategy’ in Delhi. The conference brought together senior officials from the Centre and the States to discuss the government’s counter-terrorism strategy. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan; Director, Intelligence Bureau, Mahesh Dixit; Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri; heads of Central Armed Police Forces and Central Police Organisations; Directors General of Police of 15 States and Anti-Terrorism Squad chiefs of all States and Union Territories were present. Other State police chiefs and field-level police officers joined virtually.
Improved coordination
Mr. Shah attributed the action against the network to improved coordination between security and investigating agencies. He said the government had adopted a “zero-tolerance” policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism and called for closer coordination among stakeholders to ensure there was no delay in counter-terrorism operations.
The Home Minister also said 288 fugitive criminals had been brought back to India from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026.
The PRAHAAR strategy rests on seven pillars: Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts, and Recovery and Resilience.
Mr. Shah called for the strategy to be strengthened through continuous analysis of terror incidents and said a “strong and concrete” mechanism should be developed for the next 10 years.
He also stressed that the principles of PRAHAAR should percolate down to the police station level and asked police forces to take a proactive approach. Counter-terrorism responses should be institutionalised and automated at every level of the security framework.

stories.headline: Bengaluru tree branch fall tragedy prompts Karnataka HC to script tech driven public safety framework across State
stories.deck: The public safety hazards would include trees, damaged roads, open manholes, blocked drains, exposed electrical installations, unsafe construction, encroachments, or any condition capable of causing death or serious injury, the court said.
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka High Court has issued sweeping general directions to the State government to establish a comprehensive public safety hazard detection and response mechanism, designed to digitally ensure that such dangers once reported are not lost in administrative limbo.
The public safety hazards would include trees, damaged roads, open manholes, blocked drains, exposed electrical installations, unsafe construction, encroachments, or any condition capable of causing death or serious injury, the court said.
Justice Suraj Govindaraj issued directions in his 353-page verdict on a petition granting ₹2.77 crore compensation to one Chandan G., who was paralysed after a tree branch fell on him while he was walking on a public road in Bengaluru two years ago. The 70-page directions on public safety hazard contain 52 main directions and several sub-clauses under each direction, with totally around 380 sub-clauses.
Vehicle-mounted cameras
The court also directed the State government to use existing public transport buses, garbage collection vehicles, inspection vehicles, municipal vehicles, and police and traffic vehicles fitted with cameras to identify visible public safety hazards.
Every participating vehicle and camera must be registered in the system, with certification details, installation date, and periodic recertification, and cameras must be directed toward public roads and surroundings, not private premises, the court said, while stating that every image or video must automatically record date, time, and geographical location.
The court noted that the difficulty in most cases is not the absence of statutory power, but the failure to identify, record, assess urgency, and ensure action when responsibility is divided between departments, contractors, utilities, or private owners.
Unique ID numbers
The court said that information regarding any public safety hazard enters through a common digital mechanism, even if originating from different departments. Every report or detection must receive a unique identification number with date and time of receipt, and must remain traceable from initial report until final closure.
This mechanism, the court said, must accept information from citizens, police, municipal field staff, public transport personnel, utility staff, contractors, schools, hospitals, resident associations, and fire services, and citizens should be permitted to submit photographs, videos, and location data.
Every significant public asset must progressively be assigned a unique digital asset ID, recording location, ownership, responsible authority, contractor details, warranty, complaints, repairs, and expenditure, the court said, adding that this ensures that when a hazard is detected, the system can identify not merely the location but also the authority or contractor responsible for addressing it.
Suggesting a possible hazard identification and analysis through artificial intelligence (AI), the court said that the AI report must be verified by a designated field officer and classified into four categories — emergency, high risk, medium risk, and routine.
Time-bound response
The court prescribed that the response time for emergency should be within four to 24 hours; for high risk within 24 hours; medium risk within 72 hours; and for routine, seven to 30 days. An emergency should not be placed in the ordinary administrative queue, the court clarified.
The mechanism, the court said, could be implemented in phases. Phase 1 for preparation; Phase 2 for Bengaluru city; Phase 3 for major cities including Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Shivamogga, Tumakuru, Davangere, and Ballari; and Phase 4 for State-wide implementation, to be completed in six months.
Other directions
Four-tier governance panel — apex committee, mission directorate, local committee, and local cell for monitoring.
Three-level grievance appeal mechanism for challenging detections, attribution, or penalties.
Special monsoon, night, and disaster operating modes for increased public safety risks.
Civic infrastructure health index and ease of walking score to be progressively developed.
Periodic public reporting every six months on hazards reported, verified, and rectified.
Cost of vehicle cameras ordinarily borne by vehicle-owning entities; aggregators may include it in licensing.

stories.headline: Deaths from kidney, urinary diseases in Karnataka more than triple in 10 years
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Deaths from kidney and urinary diseases more than tripled in 
Karnataka
 over the past decade, rising from 5,940 medically certified deaths in 2016 to 18,730 in 2025, as per the latest report from Medical Certification of Cause of Death (MCCD).
Total medically certified deaths rose 8%, from more than 1.4 lakh in 2016 to nearly 1.6 lakh in 2025.
Experts say the sharp rise comes amid an increase in risk factors such as diabetes, hypertension and obesity. “I think it’s a combination of many risk factors,” Dr Deepak Chitralli, consultant nephrologist at Manipal Hospital, Yeshwantpur, said, pointing to lifestyle changes. Poor management of diabetes can result in kidney damage or failure, with 40% of patients facing this threat, he added.
Kidney disease can set off a vicious cycle: impaired kidney function contributes to uncontrolled blood pressure and cardiovascular problems; cardiovascular disease worsens kidney disease.
Chitralli also flagged unsupervised use of protein supplements, especially among youngsters. “Sometimes they end up taking products that aren’t certified. They may have substances which are toxic to the kidney. In the long term, they run a high risk of mortality,” he said.
According to the MCCD report, diseases of the genitourinary system accounted for 18,730 medically certified deaths in 2025 — or 11.8% of all such deaths — making it the third-largest cause group after circulatory and respiratory diseases. The official category includes diseases of the urinary system as well as certain reproductive-system diseases.
Renal failure accounted for the overwhelming majority: 14,960 deaths, or 79.9% of deaths within the category, equivalent to 9.4% of all medically certified deaths. Men accounted for 9,530 renal-failure deaths and women for 5,430. Other disorders of the kidney and ureter accounted for 2,068 deaths.
The rise accelerated after 2018, with deaths increasing from 7,402 in 2019 to 9,884 in 2021, 13,569 in 2022, and 17,689 in 2024. The report says the share of genitourinary deaths has increased every year since 2012, barring in 2018, which saw a marginal decrease.
Renal-failure deaths were concentrated among older people. Those aged 45 and above accounted for 87.8% of such deaths, with the 70-plus group alone accounting for 5,648 deaths, or 37.7%.
The MCCD data covers nearly 1.6 lakh medically certified deaths in 2025, or 28.2% of all registered deaths. The report cautions that differences in medical-certification efficiency mean the figures may not fully represent mortality across the entire population.

stories.headline: D.K. Shivakumar petitions Defence Minister seeking land for seven projects
stories.deck: The Karnataka Chief Minister proposed development of a permanent public park and lung space on around 730 acres of defence land near the Iblur Firing Range.
stories.bodyText:
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Monday (September 28, 2026) petitioned Defence Minister Rajnath Singh seeking cooperation in expediting clearances, and sought land parcels for seven urban infrastructure and development projects in Bengaluru.
During his meeting with the Defence Minister in Delhi, the Chief Minister proposed development of a permanent public park and lung space on around 730 acres of defence land near the Iblur Firing Range. The State has proposed a public park without commercial development while the ownership will remain with the defence authorities.
Seeking a solution for 10 notified slums on about 43.83 acres of defence land, he has proposed transferring government land of equivalent area at a suitable alternative location. He has cited difficulties in identifying land of equal value within Bengaluru. The Chief Minister has also sought urgent permission for repair and redevelopment of slum areas, as monsoon rains have caused flooding.
The State has also sought review of height restrictions within a 20 km-radius of HAL airport and Yelahanka Air Force Station while balancing flight safety, and has proposed limiting mandatory NOC requirement to a 15 km-radius from the aerodrome reference point.
To ease traffic in the South-East corridor, it has sought defence land for a 24-m road connecting Lower Agaram Road, near the Government Hospital to Sarjapur Road via Ejipura Junction, which will reduce pressure on the Inner and Outer Ring Roads. The State government has already tendered and awarded the project.
Among others, the State has sought 2.039 acres of defence land for a ramp near Hebbal for the proposed Bengaluru Urban Vehicular Twin Tunnel project, permission for the tunnel to pass through defence areas near Mehkri Circle without disturbing the surface, 6.87 acres of defence land for a 18 m-link road connecting Ballari Road and Sarovara Layout, widening of the road at Mehkri Circle on Ballari Road, and 0.77 acres from DGQA and PRTC to widen the existing two lanes to three lanes to ease traffic congestion.

briefs.headline: Heart, lung diseases remain top 2 causes of deaths in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Diseases of the circulatory system continued to account for the largest share of medically certified deaths in 
Karnataka
 in 2025, while respiratory and kidney and urinary diseases together made up another quarter of such deaths, according to the state’s medical certification of cause of death (MCCD) report.
Circulatory diseases accounted for 31.1% of the nearly 1.6 lakh medically certified deaths in 2025, up from 29.4% in 2024. Ischaemic heart disease was the largest contributor, accounting for 40.8% of deaths within the circulatory disease group and 12.7% of all medically certified deaths.
Respiratory diseases were the second-largest cause group, accounting for 13.3% of medically certified deaths, marginally higher than the nearly 13.2% recorded in 2024. Kidney and urinary diseases, classified as diseases of the genitourinary system in the report, accounted for 11.8%, followed by cancer at 8.5% and digestive diseases at 7.4%.
Together, the eight leading cause groups accounted for about 87.5% of medically certified deaths in 2025. The other major groups were injuries and other external causes at 5.5%, symptoms and ill-defined conditions at 4.9%, and infectious and parasitic diseases at 4.9%.
The statistics also show a marked difference by age. Among people aged 70 and above, circulatory diseases accounted for 39.5% of deaths, followed by respiratory diseases at 17.3% and kidney and urinary diseases at 13.7%. Within the third group, renal failure accounted for 77.8% of deaths.
Among younger adults, however, external causes assumed greater importance. They accounted for 31.6% of deaths among those aged 15-24 and 20.7% among those aged 25-34, according to the report.
The report recorded nearly 1.6 lakh medically certified deaths in 2025, covering 28.2% of all registered deaths. It, however, cautioned that differences in the efficiency of medical certification across Karnataka meant the figures may not be fully representative of mortality across the entire population.
Share of medically certified deaths in 2025
■ Circulatory diseases: 31.1%
■ Respiratory diseases: 13.3%
■ Kidney & urinary diseases: 11.8%
■ Cancer: 8.5%
■ Digestive diseases: 7.4%
■ External causes: 5.5%
■ Symptoms/ill-defined causes: 4.9%
■ Infectious & parasitic diseases: 4.9%
— Source: MCCD Report-2025 | All figures rounded off

briefs.headline: Fed up with delay, Bengaluru residents ‘open’ Pink Line Metro
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Amid the inordinate delay in the opening of Pink Line, residents, frustrated with the wait, took matters into their own hands by holding a mock inauguration of the Metro line. A video clip of residents cutting a pink ribbon and holding pink balloons while ‘inaugurating’ the line at Kalena Agrahara station has gone viral on social media.
Residents of Bannerghatta Road have been demanding the opening of Pink Line for a long time. Considering the delay in construction of the underground stretch, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) plans to open the 7.5km elevated section from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere first. The remaining 13km underground section from Dairy Circle to Nagawara is slated to open next year.
The elevated section has been delayed by at least six years, at a time when traffic density on Bannerghatta Road has increased manifold. The contract for the section was issued in 2017, with a 2020 deadline for completion of the project. However, BMRCL terminated the deal after the contractor, Simplex Infrastructure, failed to deliver the project as per contractual terms.
In Aug 2021, another contractor was selected to take up the pending construction, but work took years for completion due to various issues. BMRCL set multiple deadlines to open the line, with the recent one being Sept 2026.
Many argue that opening only the elevated section will not provide much relief; the entire 21km line should be operational to benefit a larger section of commuters. Residents have also complained that the Bannerghatta Road stretch is in poor condition, with inadequate footpaths along the elevated section of Pink Line. They demanded that basic infrastructure be improved before the line is opened.
Srikanth Narasimhan, founder of Bengaluru Navanirmana Party, said, “There has been an inordinate delay in opening the Pink Line. People are frustrated with the delay. If BMRCL has received clearance to open the line, it should not wait for the PM, CM, MPs, VIPs and politicians to come and inaugurate it. Common citizens are the real VIPs. Instead of waiting for VIPs, let the common man inaugurate the line and put the Metro line to use.”
Another resident said, “BMRCL has taken over eight years to construct this line, and is still buying time to open it. The inordinate delay has caused a lot of inconvenience to the general public. People here neither have a good road nor an operational Metro line.”

briefs.headline: Karnataka High Court orders GBA to pay ₹2.77 crore to man paralysed due to falling of tree branch
briefs.deck: Rejecting the GBA’s defence that the incident was an “act of God” and that claim for compensation can be raised through a civil suit, the court said that it has power to award compensation under public law remedy
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka High Court has directed the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) to pay a compensation worth ₹2.77 crore to a 39-year-old private firm employee who became paraplegic after a Gulmohar tree branch in a private school fell on him while he was walking on a public road in 2024. The court held that the authority failed to act promptly on the school’s plea to remove the branch protruding onto the road.
Justice Suraj Govindaraj, delivering the verdict on a writ petition filed by Chandan G., held the civic body negligent for failing to act despite receiving specific prior information about the dangerous branch. The court also awarded interest at 6% on the compensation amount from the date of the incident.
Rejecting the GBA’s defence that the incident was an “act of God” and that claim for compensation can be raised through a civil suit, the court said that it has power to award compensation under public law remedy in addition to civil claim for failure to discharge a public or statutory duty by public authorities.
On March 7, 2024, Chandan was walking to work around 10 a.m. when the branch of the tree, located inside the Good Shepherd Convent School, projecting over Convent Road, broke and fell on his neck. He suffered severe spinal injuries, underwent decompression and stabilisation surgery, and was left with 85% medical disability. He claimed ₹5 crore compensation, citing permanent paraplegia and loss of earning capacity.
The school had written to the erstwhile BBMP on February 16, 2024, seeking permission to cut the branch stating that the branch “could break anytime” and was “very dangerous” to school children, residents, and vehicles. The civic body claimed that it had granted permission to prune the branch on March 7, the very day of the accident. However, the Court noted that there was no timestamp on letter of permission granted to the school.
Rejecting the BBMP’s argument that the petitioner’s claim amounted to unjust enrichment, the court adopted Motor Accident Compensation (MAC) principles to assess damages. It accepted the petitioner’s monthly salary of ₹41,212, applied MAC formula for loss of future prospects, etc., and treated his functional disability as 100% despite the 85% medical disability certificate.
The court awarded a total compensation of ₹2.82 crore, which included ₹24.44 lakh towards medical expenses, ₹1.03 for loss of future earning capacity, ₹27 lakh towards future attendant and care charges, ₹1.17 crore for future medical, physiotherapy and rehabilitation charges, and ₹10 lakh for pain, suffering and loss of amenities. The court directed the GBA to pay the remaining ₹2.77 crore to the petitioner as the civic body had paid ₹5 lakh as ex gratia earlier.
While directing the GBA to transfer the compensation amount through RTGS within twelve weeks, the court held that a payment of ₹3 lakh made by the GBA would not be deducted from the GBA’s liability while directing that the school must continue to provide free education to the petitioner’s daughter until completion of 12th standard as was promised.
Also, the court reserved liberty to the GBA to initiate legal proceedings against the school to recover any share of liability, if permissible in law, as the tree stood on its premises, while clarifying that it has not finally decided liability apportionment and has left that issue open for determination in the appropriate proceedings.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Elderly man killed in elephant attack near Mysuru Road
briefs.deck: The victim, identified as Nagaraju, was 60 years old and a resident of Anchepalya near Mysuru Road. The incident reportedly happened around 5 am on Monday in Doddabele village
briefs.bodyText:
An elderly man, who was on his morning walk with his daughter, was killed in an elephant attack near Mysuru Road, roughly about a kilometre from RajaRajeswari Medical College, near Kengeri.
The victim, identified as Nagaraju, 60, was a resident of Anchepalya off Mysuru Road. The incident reportedly happened around 5 a.m. on Monday (September 28, 2026) in Doddabele village.
Early morning alert
Sandeep Nanu, a resident of GoodEarth Malhar apartment, located near the spot, and a wildlife enthusiast, rushed to the spot at around 5.20 am after being alerted about an elephant in the vicinity and a man lying on the road, injured. On seeing the man bleeding badly, he contacted the RajaRajeswari Medical College and called for an ambulance. Parallely he also contacted the forest officials. “When I reached the spot, a few security guards were gathered around the injured person. They too had seen the elephant. However, they did not see the elephant attacking the man,” Mr. Nanu clarified.
Nagaraju who reportedly suffered a rib injury, passed away at the hospital.
Bustling area
CCTV visuals from a nearby apartment complex show the elephant on the Malhar Avenue Road, at 5:11 a.m. The street, just about 1.5 km from Mysuru Road, sees a steady flow of students, delivery personnel, school and college buses, and other people during the day.
“Nagaraju used to go on a walk every morning and walk past our house around 5.30 a.m. He had recently retired and used to work at a factory nearby earlier,” said Prema, a resident in the locality.
N.R. Kamble, Range Forest Officer, Kaggalipura Range, said that the elephant most likely reached the spot from the Bannerghatta Wildlife Division. “We reached the spot after receiving a call around 5.00 a.m. Our team is tracking the elephant,” Mr. Kamble said.
According to forest department officials, at around 7.00 am, a woman who was outside her house in Hemmigepura village, also spotted the elephant.
Mr. Kamble said that the previous sighting of elephants in the area was around 4-5 years ago. “They come from Banneghatta to BM Kaval Forest and return after 5-6 days. But, in this area, it is rare,” he said.
Reports, however, indicate that the area, years ago, used to see frequent elephant movement with herds using it as a route to move from Savanadurga to Bannerghatta forests.
Human-animal conflict
Dr. Nidhi Paliwal, a resident of GoodEarth Malhar apartments, said that during the previous elephant sighting, too, the animal was spotted on Malhar Avenue.
“CCTV visuals then showed a sighting of an elephant close to the forest area where they could go drink water from the Vrishabhavati River,” said Dr. Paliwal, who criticised the encroachments in the area.
“The BM Kaval forest area is also now encroached. The government needs to keep all these in mind when it is blindly opposing the ESA. A person has lost his life for what? He was not walking in the forest or some area where he was not supposed to. This is not something we can turn a blind eye towards or ignore for our economic gains,” she said.
Minister visits family
Following the incident Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy visited the hospital and met the family of the deceased. He announced a compensation of ₹20 lakh to the family.
In a statement issued to the media, Mr. Reddy said that elephant movement in the area had increased after the construction of a new road and the animal spotted on Monday had strayed about 5 km away from the forest area and ventured towards the city.
Combing operation
According to DCF Y. Chakrapani, the elephant is currently located inside the BM Kaval forest, and three special teams from Ramanagara, Bannerghatta, and Bengaluru Urban have been formed to conduct combing operations. Trained elephants from the Dubare division in Kodagu will also be brought in to capture the lone elephant.
“We are locating its exact coordinates. We must ensure it does not move out of that area. A team of 100 personnel is commencing the operation to capture the elephant immediately,” said Mr. Chakrapani, who also noted that steps will be taken to ensure elephants do not stray beyond the Bannerghatta division in the future.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Postal Circle to roll out more Philately Passports in four districts including Bengaluru on October 10 and 11

briefs.bodyText:
If you are a travel enthusiast, biker, philatelist or someone looking to develop new hobbies, then October is the month for you. The Karnataka Postal Circle, under the Department of Posts, will launch a new set of Philately Passports in four districts, including Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru and Belagavi, on October 10 and 11 to mark National Postal Week.
Speaking to The Hindu, a senior official from the Karnataka Postal Circle said, “We received an overwhelming response in Bengaluru
The official added, “We don’t want people to go through this hassle, so we have shared the names of venues and districts where the passports are available in advance. Besides, we don’t want people to queue up on their work day and lose time. So, passports will be sold on the second Saturday (October 10) and Sunday (October 11). Our department staff will work on these two days, though they are government holidays.”
While highlighting that the department is in the process of procuring these passports, the official noted that hundreds of enquiries have come from people through messages on social media and phone calls to post offices while some have directly come to the GPO to check availability.
“We have posted a notice at the entrance of our office and security shelters stating that the department is in the process or procuring the passports. Each passport costs ₹600. This time, we are yet to place an indent. At least 1,000 passports will be available in Bengaluru’s GPO on October 10 and 11. The number might increase as well. Similarly, there will be around 500 passports each in Mangaluru, Mysuru and Belgavi on each of these two days,” the official informed.
For the first time, the Karnataka Postal Circle has collaborated with artisans who make handcrafted Channapatna toys. The official said, “Merchandise or products, such as the letter box, keychain, and postman pen stand, will be handmade and available for sale.”
There will be also postcards carrying the picture of GI-tagged Channapatna toys and some information about the same. People can buy these postcards and write a letter to their loved ones.
What is a Philately Passport?
The Philately Passport contains 100 pictorial cancellations. It has natural, historical and cultural heritage landmarks, including Vidhana Soudha, Bannerghatta National Park in Bengaluru, Nandi Hills, Stone Chariot in Hampi, Gol Gumbaz in Vijayapura, Galaganatha Temple in Pattadakal, Chaturmukha Basadin Gerusoppa, Nagarhole National Park, Kapu Lighthouse and more.
Whenever a person visits a landmark or tourist location mentioned in this passport, they can head to the nearest designated post office and buy a postage stamp that matches the theme of the location. The postman fixes it in the passport and presses a seal of an exclusive permanent pictorial cancellation, which means the seal will be unique to that particular place.
Natarajan Venkatesan, a travel enthusiast, said, “I bought this passport in April 2026 and have been travelling to various places. Recently, I got all the 100 pictorial cancellations and submitted the passport to the post office in Bengaluru before September 30. I was told that I will be recognised for the same by the Department of Posts.”

briefs.headline: Spurious drugs racket’s kingpin arrested in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Alleged kingpin R. Prashanth was reportedly hiding in Azerbaijan after the illegal drugs case came to light
briefs.bodyText:
The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the spurious drugs racket arrested the alleged kingpin, R. Prashanth, who had been absconding and was reportedly hiding in Azerbaijan after the case came to light.
A lookout notice had been issued against Prashanth. The SIT officials arrested him at the Kempegowda International Airport when he returned to Bengaluru, investigation sources said on Monday.
The arrest was reportedly made based on the statement of another accused, Veeresh Kumar Jain, who has a shop at Minerva Circle in Bengaluru. Prashanth is being questioned by the SIT.
He was produced before Shishir R., judge of the Magadi I Additional Civil and Judicial magistrate of First Class Court, who remanded him in the police custody until October 7, 2026, for further interrogation.
The Tavarekere police in August this year raided a farm house near Bidadi and seized suspected counterfeit medicines worth around ₹5 crore, along with fake bills, injection-filling equipment, and counterfeit labels. Later, an SIT was formed to probe the network.
The alleged kingpin Prashanth managed to escape during the raid and was holed up in Azerbaijan since then.
Collaborators
Jain, a native of Rajasthan and proprietor of Krupa Healthcare near Minerva Circle in Bengaluru, was arrested by the SIT during multi-State raids conducted on September 12. He is suspected to be a close associate of the prime accused, Prashanth.
According to the investigation, Jain and Prashanth had allegedly been operating the spurious drug racket for nearly five years. The duo allegedly supplied fake medicines to major hospitals, offering the products at heavily discounted prices.
The investigators are probing their alleged operations in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Mumbai as part of the multi-State investigation.
The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration has cancelled the licences of 16 retail and wholesale pharmaceutical firms across Bengaluru and suspended those of eight others, including global pharma major Pfizer’s depot, for their alleged role in selling or supplying spurious products.

stories.headline: Piyush Goyal to hold talks for trade deal with US
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Commerce and industry minister 
Piyush Goyal
, who will visit the US for the meeting of G20 trade ministers, will meet his American counterparts to discuss the bilateral trade deal.
The two sides have been engaged on the issue but a final outcome is expected after the US unveils its future tariff strategy. It has already imposed 10-12.5% additional tariff on over 50 countries for their failure to check goods using forced labour, while the outcome of the second section 301 probe related to structural overcapacity in several countries, including India, is pending. Several analysts have argued that the next step will be unveiled after the G20 meeting in Milwaukee on Wednesday and Thursday.
In Milwaukee and Chicago, Goyal will also meet CEOs of American companies, an official statement said.

stories.headline: UAE may invest another $25bn: Piyush Goyal
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Union minister of commerce Piyush Goyal said UAE investors have expressed intent to invest another $25 billion, on the back of $25 billion already invested, with an eventual objective of taking investments in India to $100 billion.
Citing the Emirates NBD investment in RBL and IHC's acquisition of a stake in Sammaan Capital, Goyal said UAE has invested $25 billion in India and is the seventh-largest source of foreign direct investment.
"We are also exploring the possibility of UAE becoming a more important source of LPG and other energy supplies that we require. A study is also underway to see whether we can develop subsea pipelines through which gas can be transported and stored in India, strengthening our energy resilience and security," said Goyal. The two sides also discussed expanding cooperation in shipbuilding, modern ports, space technology, agri-innovation, logistics, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, energy security and fintech.
India and UAE are also discussing increasing the use of the rupee and dirham for bilateral trade. Goyal said local currency trade is currently in double digits and is expected to continue growing.
"If we have to pay for imports in dirham and receive rupee payments for exports, we can periodically convert the balances into dollars," said Goyal, addressing a press meet on Monday. 
Bankers said that since the UAE dirham is pegged to the dollar at a fixed rate, bilateral trade in local currencies is viable, liquid and low risk.
The comments came after India and UAE held the 14th meeting of the High-Level Joint Task Force on Investments, where the two sides discussed investments, trade facilitation, taxation, logistics, energy, market access and financial cooperation.
Goyal said the task force had become an effective mechanism to resolve challenges faced by investors and address issues related to the implementation of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
The CEPA is now four years old and bilateral trade has doubled to $100 billion, Goyal pointed out.

stories.headline: UAE signals another $25 billion investment in India; eyes ports, energy and space sectors: Goyal
stories.deck: India and the UAE have set a target of doubling bilateral trade to $200 billion by 2032 after trade reached around $100 billion. The target was agreed by the two countries earlier this year.
stories.bodyText:
The United Arab Emirates has indicated its intent to invest an additional $25 billion in India in the near future, Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Monday (September 28, 2026), as the two countries agreed to deepen cooperation across ports, shipbuilding, energy security, space technology and financial services.
Speaking after co-chairing the 14th India-UAE High-Level Joint Task Force on Investments with Abu Dhabi Investment Authority Managing Director Sheikh Hamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Mr. Goyal said the UAE has already invested around $25 billion in India and has a longer-term objective of taking its investments in the country to $100 billion.
“The UAE believes in India and is one of our largest foreign direct investment sources of capital. They have already invested $25 billion and are the seventh-largest source of FDI. They have also given intent to invest another $25 billion in the near future,” Mr. Goyal said.
The discussions at the task force meeting covered investments, trade facilitation, taxation, logistics, energy, market access and financial cooperation, including the use of local currencies for bilateral trade.
Mr. Goyal said the mechanism was also being used to address problems faced by investors from both countries and issues relating to the implementation of the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
India and the UAE have set a target of doubling bilateral trade to $200 billion by 2032 after trade reached around $100 billion. The target was agreed by the two countries earlier this year.
Mr. Goyal pointed to recent investments by UAE entities as evidence of growing investor interest, including Emirates NBD’s acquisition of a majority stake in RBL Bank and International Holding Company’s investment in Sammaan Capital.
Emirates NBD completed its investment of around $2.75 billion in RBL Bank in June after securing regulatory approvals, while IHC has committed around $1 billion to acquire a controlling stake in Sammaan Capital.
A major outcome of Monday’s discussions was an agreement to establish a bilateral working group covering six areas of maritime cooperation — ship ownership, development of modern ports, ship manufacturing, repair and maintenance, ship breaking and container manufacturing.
“They are looking at ports, they are looking at shipbuilding, they are looking at greater investments in space and our startups,” Mr. Goyal said, adding that UAE investors were also interested in India’s stock markets.
Mr. Goyal said India’s port capacity had doubled over the past decade and would need to double again over the next 10 years as the economy expands.
He said UAE investors could participate in new ports as well as the expansion of existing facilities, specifically referring to the upcoming Vadhavan port in Maharashtra and port projects along India’s eastern and western coasts.
“I think there is tremendous potential for mutual cooperation between UAE and India,” he said.
Energy security was another major area discussed by the two sides. Mr. Goyal said India was working with the UAE on expanding strategic petroleum reserves in the country, with studies currently underway.
“We’ll be seeing significant ramp-up of investments from UAE in this area,” he said.
India is also exploring increased supplies of LNG and other gases from the UAE, while a study is examining the feasibility of subsea pipelines that could transport gas to India, Mr. Goyal said.
The proposals come against the backdrop of heightened geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia and pressure on global energy and shipping routes. Mr. Goyal, however, said geopolitical and strategic issues themselves were not discussed by the investment task force.
The two sides also discussed expanding cooperation in artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, fintech, food security and agri-innovation.
In space technology, India and the UAE are exploring greater investment and cooperation involving startups, including companies working on technologies related to orbital debris. In fintech, discussions included using India’s digital payments capabilities alongside artificial intelligence and cybersecurity to expand financial services cooperation.
Mr. Goyal also said greater cooperation in food processing, packaging, quality control and branding could help Indian farmers and MSMEs increase exports of food and marine products to the Gulf and other international markets.
On India’s broader export performance, the minister said merchandise exports had grown by more than 15% in the current financial year up to September 21, describing the figure as an “informal data point” ahead of the release of final official numbers next month.
India recorded exports of goods and services worth around $863 billion last year and has set a target of reaching $1 trillion this year, Mr. Goyal said.
He also highlighted the role of India’s expanding network of free-trade agreements, saying that agreements with developed economies were intended to provide Indian farmers, fishermen, MSMEs and manufacturers preferential access to larger overseas markets.
Civil aviation was not a main focus of Monday’s investment task force meeting, Mr. Goyal said, but discussions between India’s relevant ministries and the UAE continued to improve cooperation and business opportunities in the sector.
Mr. Goyal said the breadth of discussions reflected the expanding economic relationship between the two countries, noting that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan had met four times over the past year.

stories.headline: Lupin gets U.S. FDA tentative nod for Apixaban Oral Suspension
stories.bodyText:
Generic drugmaker Lupin has received tentative approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its new drug application for Apixaban Oral Suspension 1.25mg/mL.
The approval was obtained through the 505(b)(2), new drug approval, pathway of the regulator. Upon final approval, the product will be manufactured at its Somerset, New Jersey facility, thereby leveraging the company’s U.S.-based manufacturing expertise, Lupin said.
The approved product is an oral liquid formulation of apixaban, the active ingredient in Eliquis (apixaban) of Bristol Myers Squibb and provides an alternative administration option for adult patients requiring anticoagulation therapy, including those who may have difficulty swallowing tablets.
Apixaban oral suspension expands the ways in which this important therapy could be administered, while reinforcing our commitment to building a differentiated portfolio, CEO Vinita Gupta said.
